message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loved the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and most of all, they loved houses. The nicely laid out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. The first few attempts were disastrous, with walls crumbling and roofs collapsing into the dirt below. Pebble Spring watched the village masons with great interest, studying how they mixed mortar and aligned stones. Each morning, they climbed to the highest point of the construction site to observe the progress. The villagers at first regarded the strange creature with suspicion, but curiosity soon won over fear. A young apprentice named Tom became Pebble Spring's closest friend among the humans. Tom would share his bread and cheese with the Leshy in exchange for small magical tricks. Together, they worked on a modest cottage at the edge of the village square. The walls of the cottage glowed faintly with residual enchantments, a subtle purple hue in the twilight. Pebble Spring was particularly proud of the arched doorway they had crafted with flowing gestures. The other masons began to incorporate the Leshy's methods into their own daily work. A gentle magic in the joints meant the stones held together without the need for excess mortar. The village slowly transformed as more houses adopted the distinctive new style. Roofs were shaped like gentle waves, and chimneys spiraled like vines climbing toward the sky. Children would chase Pebble Spring through the cobblestone streets, laughing and shouting as the creature danced. The elder mason, a gruff woman named Martha, finally grudgingly accepted the Leshy's remarkable talent. She called the new architectural style "springwork," and the term stuck in the village dialect. By autumn, the village had become a destination for travelers from distant and foreign lands. They came to admire the unique houses and to learn the secret blend of magic and stone. Pebble Spring felt a profound sense of belonging that no other settlement had ever offered them. The small creature that had been sleeping peacefully on the warm windowsill all morning suddenly opened its bright green eyes and blinked slowly at the garden outside where the colorful flowers were all notably spotty.
